model_reviews.who: Hassana Labs (Leon Chlon), by a reinforcement-learning "verified debate" model over one weekend
model_reviews.what: Reports 44 issues in the 940-page draft, 23 of them not raised in any public review before, each with a proposed repair: 15 repairs proved in Lean, 5 with key pieces in Lean, 2 on paper, 1 absorbed by another. Gives what it calls an exact diagnosis, proved in Lean: in the corrected trace formula behind Theorem 12.5.1.1 the remainder is independent of the strip width if and only if every zero lies on Re = 1/2, so the argument's central step is equivalent to its conclusion. Confirms that section 12.3 reads "Include section", that the proof of 10.4.2.8 ends "Return here and complete proof", and that Theorem 13.3.1.2 has no statement. Reports new mathematics built alongside: the geometric side in the operator order P∘A at every finite rank, the missing section 12.3 decomposition, a nuclearity bound, a spectral converse, and foundations; about 80,000 lines of Lean in all. Of the nine results the argument relies on, each is listed with what is proved and what is "not yet", including: no continuation and functional equation for number fields other than Q; the identity of P∘A(h) with the assembled operator not yet proved; Theorem 12.4.1.1 as a whole not yet stated. Opens by congratulating the author. Lean 4.27.0-rc1, Mathlib commit fdddb3e; 1,506 declarations named, 1,393 with receipts showing exit code 0 and the three standard axioms, 26 turned back by their compile service for linter warnings only, 87 definitions inside checked files. Each source is a standalone compilation unit; the README says different sources may declare the same names.
model_reviews.note: The reader is a model and the signature is a company's, so this is a report, not a read cycle: it does not close the reading gap, and it is not a specialist's check of anything. What the Lean checks is the reviewers' own statements, not the manuscript's: the key theorem, remainder_independent_iff_critical_line in lean/spectral/Proof-28b15828da3e/Proof.lean (receipt-1.json: exit code 0, 106 s, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; source hash matches), is about an arbitrary entire function f with a zero count O(R log R), takes the corrected trace formula as a hypothesis in the form "the sum over zeros within width a of the line tends to G minus remainder(a)", and concludes that the remainder is the same for all widths if and only if f has no zero off the line. Read plainly: if the trace formula is of that form, then the step the draft would need is a restatement of the conclusion. The Chapter 13 statement for K = Q, chapter13_paired_control_iff_riemannHypothesis, is likewise conditional on an interface (Chapter13RegularizedLimit D) and concludes Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis from a control condition and back. Both are machine-checked diagnoses of the argument's shape; neither proves or refutes the trace formula on the draft's actual objects. On this record: no formal deduction of the main theorem exists (EG1 unchanged); no independent mathematician has read the draft under their name (EG2 unchanged); the author has not released Chapter 13 (EG3 unchanged, and the report confirms the placeholders page by page); the trace-formula dispute now has a public, specific form, that 12.5.1.1 sums only interior zeros while the trace it cites runs over the closed strip, with the equivalence above as its consequence, though this is a structural defect and not the numerical counterexample reported on the Zulip (EG4 remains open on that ask); the appendix errata have a second, larger list beside them, 21 of the 44 overlapping earlier reports, still unchecked by a specialist (EG5 unchanged). The report's own list of what is "not yet" proved is the honest part of the page and is the part this record relies on. A rerun of the 531 standalone sources under a pre-registration is feasible and would make the receipts a second-party fact; it has not been done. The note is one of about ten outside reports on the draft indexed at github.com/mccorvie/riemann-masullo/blob/main/OUTSIDE_REPORTS.md (Yonemoto, Nielsen, Golub/Refine, Nayebi, Goyal, Naslund, Baez and others), most of them AI-generated and most dated 20 to 22 November; this one carries the largest Lean component.

public_readings.who: J. L. Nielsen, Center for Topological Physics, Lawrence, Kansas (a physicist and philosopher of science by her public profiles)
public_readings.title: The Invalidity of Alpöge's Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis: vacuously true geometric and lattice witnesses in the Lean formalization
public_readings.versions: the record's version history could not be read; a search index reported sixteen uploads between 20 and 22 November, the title moving between "Proof" and "Proposed Proof"
public_readings.what: concludes that the release does not contain a proof. Concedes that the top-level theorem has Mathlib's type RiemannHypothesis and that the source has no axiom, sorry or native_decide. Reports, from about 70 of the 175,187 files read in the community mirror at commit 712a6aef (archive sha256 9631b4f0…, matching this record's pin), that the proof's live route passes a hypothesis bundle whose geometric predicate is defined as True (anyGeometry, closed under GeoCl), that the lattice-side equalities hold by rfl because the witness is a copy of the row-side data, that the divisor height is set by definition to an explicit formula and its defining equation proved by rfl, that the map from lattices to sections is the zero map, and that the lemmas written to extract geometric content are never called. From this she argues that the inequality meant to trap an independent geometric height compares a quantity with itself, so that the term certifies only "RiemannHypothesis = RiemannHypothesis". An appendix states the kernel objection and answers that no independent algebraic route remains once the vacuous package is removed. Offers one check, a transitivelyUsedConstants walk from riemannHypothesis, which would list the constants the term uses.
public_readings.note: A reading of the formal term by a named person, the first on the public record to dispute the claim. Its factual reports about the source are not checked here. Its conclusion does not follow from them as stated. A closed term of Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis, accepted by the kernel with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, is a proof of that proposition whatever the names of the intermediate hypotheses say: a hypothesis slot defined as True removes an assumption and weakens nothing downstream; an equation proved by rfl is an equation; and RiemannHypothesis is a statement about the zeros of zeta, not a proposition that is definitionally True, so no term of that type is the identity "RH = RH". The paper names no error in the statement, the pins or the kernels, and gives no mechanism by which the type could be inhabited without the proposition holding. What it does report, if its citations are right, is that the formal route does not use the geometric content the archive's names advertise. Jaswal's guide, read the same day, notes the same True-valued slots (hypotheses of TopShapeAlt set to True; a bundle field of type UnusedSlot72, which is True) and treats them as unused inputs. That is a finding about what the proof actually does and how it can be read, which bears on the reading gap and not on the machine check. The offered dependency walk would confirm which constants the term uses, not whether the proof holds, and is not run here. Standing unchanged.

public_reactions.what: Lists four "stupid things I did". The figure of 250,000+ pages was a joke; he finds big numbers funny and did not correct it in the days after the announcement. He did not want any "slop writeup" attached to the problem, judged he could not produce a readable account, and "went off the Lean to lengthmaxx". The Lean is "full of garbage obviously, but compiles"; criticism of it is reasonable; he should have cleaned it up and found that hard "for various strange reasons". He was "yoloing a lot in there", bets most of it is unnecessary, and expects it to simplify massively. His stated point: arguments like these are raw inputs for interpolating definitions; there is no H^1 object over number fields yet; Riemann should be easy, and any real difficulty indicates the current setup is wrong.
public_reactions.note: The claimant's own account of the artifact. It changes nothing about correctness: the main theorem's type and the kernel's acceptance (finding F1) are facts about the archive, not about its author's tidiness, and the Lean and Mathlib communities' statement of 21 November stands. It changes three things about how the rest of this record should be read. First, the 250,000-page document that several readings, this record's own notes and the public ask for an attempt record referred to does not exist as described; what record of attempts exists, and in what form, is unknown, and the ask is now for whatever that record is. Second, the archive's size carries no information about effort or method by the author's own statement, which agrees with what the traces measured without knowing it: a third of the archive's constants unused, rewrite marks on 33 of 81 hinges, the chain shape, the author's own expectation that "most is unnecessary". The shape traces measured a deliberately uncleaned artifact and should be read as such; the dominator tree is still the tree of what the kernel uses. Third, point 4 is the author's statement of what the proof means to him, a band-three statement that belongs beside Jerby's and Saha's and carries no standing.
